title: Two-slope fits gave a larger mean warm than cold ENSO sea-level slope at two Pacific gauges in 1961-2025
abstract: We tested whether winter sea level has different response slopes in warm and cold ENSO phases at San Francisco and Seattle. We used 62 common complete winters in 1961-2025. A continuous two-slope model included a linear time trend. The mean warm-minus-cold slope was 4.57 cm per C. Its 95% five-year block interval was 0.19 to 8.37 cm per C. The interval excludes zero. Removing the three preselected strong winters reduced the difference and left an interval that includes zero. Two fixed gauges, missing records, a fixed ENSO anomaly reference, few strong events, and unmeasured wind and pressure limit inference. This is an association test, not a cause or forecast test. The package preserves source hashes, used monthly fields, seasonal values, code, uncertainty draws, sensitivity checks, and figures.
